headline: Counterfactual re-execution improves reported robot recovery supervision from ambiguous failures
summary: MAGMA-GEN uses a privileged coach to suggest localized corrections or recovery actions after an ambiguous robotic failure, then re-executes each candidate from the same simulator state and retains it only when downstream progress improves. In the authors’ simulated manipulation evaluation, four generation runs report a 26.25% mean recovery rate versus 16.66% for the strongest Best-of-N retry baseline and a 16.79% complete-task success rate versus 14.15%. With branching factor B=2, the authors report 15/30 real-robot trials succeeded, compared with 12/30 for expert-rollout distillation and 11/30 for CLEANER-adapted; each method used one checkpoint, so the small physical trial does not establish statistical superiority. The paper reports a bounded mechanism and transfer feasibility, not robust long-horizon robotics. The linked repository is now a v2 beta while the paper describes software v0.1; exact version correspondence and independent reproduction remain open.
